headline: India, Nepal, Indonesia achieve zero rhino poaching in 2025
meta_description: India, Nepal and Indonesia reported zero rhino poaching in 2025, a major conservation milestone for Asia's most threatened greater one-horned rhinos.
summary_short: Three Asian nations hit a remarkable conservation milestone: zero rhino poaching cases in 2025. Greater one-horned rhinos are among the continent's most vulnerable speci…
body:
India, Nepal and Indonesia reported zero rhino poaching in 2025, marking a major conservation milestone for some of Asia's most threatened rhinos.

The greater one-horned rhino, one of the species most at risk across the continent, has been the focus of intensive protection efforts across these three nations. This achievement represents a significant breakthrough after years of habitat loss and illegal hunting that had devastated rhino populations throughout the region.

The convergence of zero poaching cases across multiple countries in a single year demonstrates what coordinated conservation work can accomplish. While challenges remain, this milestone offers genuine hope for the future of Asia's rhinos and the ecosystems they inhabit.
quick_facts: India, Nepal, and Indonesia recorded zero rhino poaching in 2025
Greater one-horned rhino is among Asia's most threatened species
Major conservation milestone for regional wildlife protection
